old_caption: The video captures a dynamic scene where an orange frisbee is thrown towards a stationary red Coca-Cola can placed on top of a white cylindrical object, likely a bollard or post. The background features a blurred outdoor setting with trees and a building, suggesting a park or urban environment. As the frisbee approaches the can, it collides with it at high speed, causing the can to spin rapidly and eventually explode. The impact sends the frisbee flying off to the side, while the can bursts open, spraying liquid and debris into the air. The liquid splashes outward in a dramatic arc, creating a cloud of mist and droplets that obscure part of the scene momentarily. The camera remains stationary throughout, focusing on the interaction between the frisbee and the can, capturing the explosive moment in slow motion to emphasize the force and energy involved.

caption: The video captures a slow-motion close-up of a splash already underway, with a tilted translucent orange disc set against a crushed red Coca-Cola can above a pale rounded dome at the bottom. Brown cola and white spray surround the disc, while a blurred tree trunk and fence remain fixed in the softly lit background. During the sequence, the disc tilts and slides leftward, its printed star logo staying visible on the surface. The can rotates in place, bringing its silver base and barcode label from the upper left toward the lower left as the red body remains crumpled. The liquid cloud thickens to the right of the disc and behind it, then breaks into finer droplets as the objects continue their leftward drift. The disc is nearly off the left edge, the can still turns amid the spray, and the splash remains unsettled.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.

prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
